# Books

A Quarto book gets one index for the whole book, not one per chapter — and
every index the book declares, in every format, each printed where its own
marker stands. See [Named indexes](named-indexes.qmd) for how a book declares
more than one. Write the placement marker in the chapter that should hold it:

```markdown
::: {.qi-index-here}
:::
```

Everything below, down to the last section, is about the **HTML book**: it is
the one Quarto renders a chapter at a time. A PDF or EPUB book goes through a
single Pandoc process, so none of it applies — see the last section.

**Put that chapter last.** Quarto renders an HTML book's chapters in order,
and each chapter is a separate render that cannot see the others, so the index
is built from the chapters that ran before the one holding the marker. Put the
marker anywhere else and the chapters after it are represented by whatever the
*previous* render recorded: on a first render they are read back from their own
sources, without the links into their pages that a record carries, and after an
edit their entries can name terms the chapter no longer marks and link to
anchors its page no longer has. The extension names those chapters every time
it builds the index, so this is loud rather than silent — but the fix is to
move the marker, not to render twice.

In the HTML book, each entry's locators link to the chapters that mark the
term, in book order — across files, and across subdirectories, from wherever
the index chapter sits. A cross-reference links to its target entry whenever
some chapter in the book contributes it, so `see=` works across chapters
exactly as it does inside one document.

A book that declares several indexes prints each index some chapter files a
mark in, each at the first marker naming it — in whichever chapter that marker
stands — and any index no marker names after them, in declared order, at the
end of the book's last chapter. Every judgement the extension makes across
chapters is made inside one index, so a `see=` written in one index that names
a term only another index marks is reported as naming nothing indexed, and the
report says which index it was judged in.

The last chapter is where an index no marker names goes whatever the book's
markers say, provided some chapter of the book places an index at all. That
chapter is the end of the book's own chapter list, which every chapter of
every render reads the same way, so which chapter carries the section does not
change from one render to the next. Where the last chapter carries a marker of
its own, the section follows the ones its markers place; where it carries
none, the section goes at the end of that chapter. A book with no marker
anywhere places no index and grows no section in its last chapter either.

Adding or moving a placement marker takes effect on the very next render: a
chapter that gains a marker for an index prints that index from then on. An
index no marker names stays in the last chapter throughout — unless the marker
you add or remove is the book's only one, since the proviso above turns every
such section on or off with it.

Two things worth knowing:

- **Render the whole book when you publish.** Rendering a single chapter
  updates that chapter's marks only; the index is rebuilt from what the last
  full render recorded for the others. `quarto render` with no file argument
  is what makes the index current.
- **A book with marks but no marker chapter gets no index**, and says so once
  per render, naming the marker to add. The extension will not choose a
  chapter for you.

Each chapter records its marks in `.quarto/quarto-index/` inside your project —
Quarto's own scratch directory, alongside the caches Quarto keeps there, and
never copied into `_book/`. There is nothing to configure. A project created
with `quarto create project` already ignores `/.quarto/` in git; a book whose
`_quarto.yml` you wrote by hand may not, and that one line is worth adding.

If a chapter's record cannot be written or read back — a read-only project
tree, a stale file where the directory belongs, a record left by an older
version of this extension — the book still renders, and the extension names
the chapter the report is about. Rendering that chapter again is the fix. A
record that names an index you have since removed from `indexes:` costs
nothing: its marks are filed in the first index the book still declares, and
the report names the chapter and the name.

Where the record was there to open and could not be used, that chapter's own
`.qmd` is read and parsed instead, and the terms it marks — and the placement
markers it carries — join the book's index. The report says so: it names the
chapter and says its terms came from that chapter's source rather than from a
record. Where the source parses and carries no mark this route can reach — a
chapter whose marks all arrive through an include, say — the report says that
instead, so nothing tells you terms came back when none did.

What comes back is what you wrote. An `entry=` naming several levels rebuilds
its sub-entry and the parent it hangs under; a `sort=` still files the term
where it asks; and `see=` and `see-also=` still print their lines, neither
carrying a page number, as neither does on an ordinary render. What does not
come back is anything the chapter worked out for itself while it rendered.

Five things recovery does not return.

- **No fragment.** A recovered term links to the chapter's page and nothing
  after it, so following it lands at the top of that page rather than at the
  marked passage. The id a mark is anchored at is minted while that chapter
  renders, and only its record carries it.
- **Nothing that reaches the chapter through an include shortcode or an
  executed cell.** Quarto expands both before any filter runs, and what is
  read here is the file on disk.
- **Nothing inside a block or span carrying `.content-visible` or
  `.content-hidden`.** Quarto settles those by the format being rendered, the
  active profile, or a metadata value, and the file on disk records none of
  that — so recovery takes such a block or span out whole, whatever its
  `when-` or `unless-` attributes say. A term marked inside one is left out
  even where this render would have printed it.
- **Nothing at all, where Pandoc's markdown reader cannot read the chapter
  source.** The report then says the source could not be read either, and that
  chapter's terms are missing from the index until it is rendered again.
- **A page range, and a principal locator.** Whether two marks are the two ends
  of one range, and which locator a `mention="principal"` emphasizes, are
  settled inside that chapter's own render against the anchors it produced. A
  recovered mark indexes as though `range=` and `mention=` were absent: both
  ends of a range print the one page the chapter is on, and the role prints as
  an undeclared one does.

A record that is simply *absent* — a chapter no render has written one for —
is read back only where its terms would otherwise be lost from a section this
chapter itself prints. Two chapters qualify, and between them they are every
chapter that can print one: a chapter carrying a placement marker of its own,
and the book's last chapter, which takes on every index no marker names. Both
read the sources of the chapters no record has been written for, and every
other chapter reads such a record as absent and says nothing about it.

So a book rendered chapter by chapter, or into a tree whose records never
survive, still prints an index carrying every chapter's terms rather than one
short of them — with the same limits every recovered chapter carries, the
missing fragment among them. A whole-book render is unaffected, because by the
time a chapter reads the store the chapters before it have written their
records: the ordinary first render of a book whose marker sits in its last
chapter reads no source at all and says nothing.

A chapter with no record whose source parses and reaches no index mark is
passed over in silence. It has lost nothing — a chapter that marks nothing
looks exactly like this — and reporting it would say so for most of a correct
book on every render. Where the source cannot be read at all, the report
naming that outcome is drawn, as it is for a record that was written.

One case that looks absent and is not: a record that is *there* and cannot be
opened. What tells the two apart is the listing of the directory the record
belongs in — a record whose filename is among that directory's entries was
written there, whatever opening it does, so it is out of reach rather than
unwritten and its chapter is read back from its source. That covers one record
whose permissions have been cleared, a store directory that has lost the search
bit its records are opened through, and the store directory itself being out of
reach — replaced by a file, or with its read permission gone — where every
record under it is out of reach and every chapter is read back. The book still
gets a complete index, with the unusable-record report drawn for each such
chapter by every chapter that looks for its record. The fix is whichever put
the path out of reach: taking away whatever stands in its place, or restoring
permissions.

The listing is the only evidence there is, so a file merely *named* like a
record and unopenable counts as one that was written — a broken symlink left at
that path by hand, say. Nothing this extension writes produces a file of that
name it cannot open, so the case arises only where something else made it, and
what it costs is a chapter read back from its source rather than dropped. A
record whose name the directory does not list is absent exactly as before.

The reports repeat on rules of their own. The one for a record no render has
written is drawn by every chapter the paragraph above admits — a chapter with a
placement marker, and the book's last chapter — once for each such record it
meets. The one for a record that could not be read is drawn by every chapter
that opens it — every chapter of the book
but the one whose record it is, since a chapter reads the store before it
writes its own. The one for a record left by a different version of this
extension is drawn once for every chapter that builds an index section, which
is what that record costs it; a chapter that builds none draws it too where the
records it read show no chapter of the book placing an index — a book with no
placement marker anywhere, and equally a chapter rendered while the record of
the chapter carrying the marker cannot itself be read.

## The merged books: PDF and EPUB

A PDF book and an EPUB book need none of the above. Quarto renders each as one
merged document, so the extension sees every chapter's marks at once: there is
no per-chapter record, nothing to keep current, and the marker may go in any
chapter. A PDF book's `makeindex` has always had every chapter's marks at once,
and the printed index gathers page numbers from all of them. An EPUB book
prints every index its `indexes:` metadata declares, each under its own title,
and a page range opened in one chapter and closed in another pairs — see the
[EPUB](epub.qmd) page.
